database.description: The {@link AwsAthenaDatabase database} this table belongs to.

sourceS3Url.description:
The source data folder on s3 for this table.

Example: 's3://bucket/path/to/data/folder/'

dataFormat.description:
Format of the source data on S3. Currently supported formats of source files are {@link ContentType#csv},
{@link ContentType#json}, and {@link ContentType#plainText}. Please note that if using {@link ContentType#json}
as source data format, one record should be written in one line.
i.e. `{"name": "Jay", "age": 28, "phone": "515-554-5573"}`
     `{"name": "Amy", "age": 56, "phone": "555-355-7755"}`

sourceEncrypted.description: If provided source data on s3 is encrypted.

columns.description:
An array of pairs for definition of column name and its value type in this table. The 1st element in pair stands
for the name of the column, the 2nd element in pair stands for the value type of the column. The order of column in
the created table is positioned based by the element in the array of pairs.

Example: [{{"name"}, {"string"}}, {{"age"}, {"int"}}, {{"phone"}, {"string"}}]

terminators.description:
If the dataFormat is {@link ContentType#plainText}, terminators should be provided to terminate fields, collections
and map keys. Currently ONLY field terminator is supported because Aws Athena Jdbc driver does not support reading
array and map type data.

The input is index based, i.e.

| Index | Terminator           |   default   |
|-------|----------------------|-------------|
|  0    |   Field terminator   |     ","     |
|  1    | Collection terminator| "undefined" |
|  2    | Map Key terminator   | "undefined" |

Note that ";" is line terminator in Hive DDL, please add a escape symbol '\' before it. And if a terminator is not
used in the source data, it is ok to pass "undefined" as an entry in the terminators.

Example: ["\;", "undefined", "undefined"], ";" -> field terminator, "undefined" -> collection terminator,
                                                  "undefined" -> map key terminator

targetType.description:
If target type is provided, the table will be constructed based on fields defined in the given target type
(i.e, each field in the target type would be one column in the table.) and data type of each column is based on the
type of the field in the given target type. The following mapping shows currently supported field types.

|         Fields type of the C3 target type     |          Data type of the column on Athena table                |
|-----------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
|{@link PrimitiveType primitive}                |                        as original primitive type               |
|{@link Boolean boolean}                        |                          string type                            |
|{@link Persistable persistable} reference type |                string type for the id of reference instance     |
|    other types                                |      string type, and only reads value as string when queried   |

partition.description:
An array of pair for the definition of partition key and its value type. The 1st element in pair stands
for the name of the partition, the 2nd element in pair stands for the value type of the partition key.
The order of partitions is positioned based by the element in the given array.

Example: if a table uses "year", "month" and "location" as partition key, then these three keys SHOULD NOT be
         included in {@link AwsAthenaTable#columns} but in {@link AwsAthenaTable#partition} when creating a table.
         The source data folder on s3 then should have the folder structure like the following, and the table should
         specify {@link AwsAthenaTable#sourceS3Url} as "s3://bucket/data/" when created in this example.

          s3://bucket/data/year=2014/month=02/location=England/data0.txt
          s3://bucket/data/year=2015/month=02/location=England/data1.txt
          s3://bucket/data/year=2015/month=03/location=USA/data0.txt
          s3://bucket/data/year=2015/month=04/location=England/data0.txt
          s3://bucket/data/year=2016/month=05/location=France/data0.txt
          s3://bucket/data/year=2016/month=06/location=Japan/data0.txt

If some fields are used as a partition keys in {@link AwsAthenaTable#targetType}, those keys will automatically
be removed from the columns of created table. Please note that source file on s3 should not contain data of these
partition keys, Aws Athena would get the value from s3 url path when doing query.

Data partition helps to reduce unnecessary data scanning, cost and improve performance. In this example, scanning
would only happen in folder "s3://bucket/data/year=2015/month=03/location=USA/" with query like
"SELECT * FROM <table> WHERE location=USA".

title:
AwsAthenaTable represents a table under a {@link AwsAthenaDatabase database} on Aws Athena. The data source of Athena
only comes from Aws S3. Note that table names and database names are all case-INSENSITIVE on Athena.
